feed.title: NPR Topics: Politics
feed.subtitle: Follow NPR Politics for nonpartisan coverage of government, elections, policy debates and voting rights. Plus weekday audio from The NPR Politics Podcast.

entry.title: Hegseth has remained defiant as Congress members deliberate articles of impeachment
entry.summary: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is fighting back. As members of Congress begin deliberating on the articles of impeachment against him, Hegseth gave his first press conference in months.

entry.title: House votes to effectively end the impeachment effort against Pete Hegseth
entry.summary: House Republicans managed to short-circuit a floor vote on the impeachment effort brought against the Defense Secretary by Kentucky Republican Thomas Massie.

entry.title: Supreme Court seems split over federal agencies' ability to fine for law violations
entry.summary: The Supreme Court heard arguments Tuesday in a case related to temporary worker visas. The company involved says enforcement issues should go through the courts, not the federal agency alone.

entry.title: House Republicans elect Jim Jordan as their next leader
entry.summary: House GOP lawmakers have chosen Ohio's Jim Jordan to serve as minority leader, elevating a co-founder of the ultra-conservative Freedom Caucus to succeed Mike Johnson as the chamber's top Republican.

entry.title: House GOP faults the federal government for failing to hold Epstein accountable
entry.summary: The House Oversight Committee has released a report into its investigation into sex-offender, Jeffrey Epstein. They faulted the federal government for not holding the financier accountable.

entry.title: House set to vote to impeach Hegseth. And, SCOTUS allows border wall work to proceed
entry.summary: The House could vote to impeach Hegseth, but removing him from office will be tough. And, SCOTUS ruled that a federal judge did not have the authority to halt border wall construction.

entry.title: Former Pentagon spokesman on articles of impeachment filed against Hegseth
entry.summary: NPR's Steve Inskeep speaks with former Pentagon spokesman John Ullyot about articles of impeachment brought against Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth.

entry.title: Why did California's billionaire tax fail to surf the blue wave?
entry.summary: Two economists debate what California's vote on Prop 40 means for the wealth tax movement.

entry.title: House GOP elects Jim Jordan as new leader as the party looks to rebuild from midterms
entry.summary: Jordan, a close Trump ally and co-founder of the ultra-conservative House Freedom Caucus, will succeed Mike Johnson, who says he's stepping down as the chamber's top Republican.

entry.title: The Democratic Party gained power across the country in the midterms. Now what?
entry.summary: Voters handed Democrats the keys to power across the country and expect them to drive in a different direction. Party leaders are now trying to figure out which way to go.
